Hohe Weide Synagogue in Hamburg

Synagogue · Hamburg, Germany

The Hohe Weide Synagogue was inaugurated on 9 September 1960 and became the principal postwar synagogue of the Jewish Community of Hamburg. The building was designed by architects Karl Heinz Wongel and Klaus May. It continues to serve its original Jewish religious role: the Central Council of Jews in Germany lists services and a mikveh at this address and identifies the community's orientation as Orthodox. Visits and educational tours are arranged through the Jewish Community rather than through published general opening hours.
